html-b13-link-targets.q: You are linking from your article to an external reference and want readers to keep your article open. Which markup is correct and safe?
html-b13-link-targets.why: target="_blank" (with the underscore) opens a new tab, and rel="noopener" prevents the destination from getting a scripting handle on your page. 'blank' without the underscore creates a named window instead.

html-b13-link-targets.q:
A 'Back to top' button at the bottom of a long page should scroll to the h1, which reads

Guide

. What href does the button's link need?
html-b13-link-targets.why: Fragment links start with # followed by the target element's id. href="top" would try to load a file called 'top', and _top is a target keyword for frames, not an href.

html-b13-link-targets.q: You want a 'Download brochure' link that saves brochure.pdf instead of opening it in the browser tab. Which markup does that?
html-b13-link-targets.why: The download attribute on a normal href link tells the browser to save the file rather than navigate to it. Links use href (not src), and there is no _download target or download: scheme.

html-b14-images.q: A news article includes a photo of flooding that the text refers to. Which alt text is right?
options: alt="Flooded main street with cars submerged to their windows"
alt="image of a photo of a flood picture"
html-b14-images.why: Meaningful images get a concise description of their content. Empty alt is only for decoration, and phrases like 'image of' are redundant because screen readers already announce it as an image.

html-b14-images.q: Your page visibly jumps as each photo loads, pushing the text down. What is the standard HTML fix?
options: Convert every image to PNG format
Add width and height attributes so the browser reserves space before the file arrives
Move all images to the bottom of the page
Add title attributes to each image
html-b14-images.why: With width and height declared, the browser knows each image's proportions immediately and reserves a correctly sized box, eliminating layout shift. Format, position and tooltips do not affect it.

html-b14-images.q: You need a company logo that must stay pin-sharp at every size, from a 16px favicon to a conference banner. Which format fits best?
options: GIF, because it is widely supported
SVG, because it describes shapes and scales without pixelation
AVIF, because it is the newest format
html-b14-images.why: SVG stores geometry rather than pixels, so it renders sharply at any size — ideal for logos and icons. JPG, GIF and AVIF are raster formats that blur when scaled up.

html-b15-figure-favicon.q: A report page shows a chart with 'Figure 3: Quarterly revenue' beneath it. How should the pair be marked up so the caption is structurally attached?
options: containing the with the caption in its title attribute
html-b15-figure-favicon.why: figure groups self-contained content with its figcaption, making the relationship machine-readable. A styled paragraph only looks attached, and <caption> belongs exclusively to tables.

html-b15-figure-favicon.q: An image map's clickable areas are not working. The map is declared as <map name="plan">. What must the img element carry?
html-b15-figure-favicon.why: The img references the map through usemap with a # prefix, while the map itself declares its name without one — the mismatch convention that most often breaks image maps.

html-b15-figure-favicon.q: You add <link rel="icon" href="favicon.png"> to a page. Where will visitors actually see that icon?
options: In the top-left corner of the page body
In the browser tab, bookmarks and history entries
html-b15-figure-favicon.why: The favicon is browser chrome, not page content: it labels the tab, bookmark lists and history. It never renders inside the page and needs no CSS.

html-b16-lists.q: You are marking up the steps to reset a router, where doing them out of order fails. Which list is correct?
options: <ul>, because bullets look cleaner for instructions
html-b16-lists.why: Order matters, so the list is ordered — ol renumbers itself automatically when steps change. Hand-typed numbers in paragraphs go stale, and ul signals that order is irrelevant.

html-b16-lists.q: Steps 1-3 appear under one heading and the procedure continues under the next heading. How do you make the second list begin at step 4?
html-b16-lists.why: The start attribute sets an ol's first number. type controls the numbering style (letters, Roman numerals), and there is no continue attribute in HTML.

html-b16-lists.q: A packing item 'Toiletries' needs its own sub-list of three items. Where does the inner <ul> go?
options: Directly between the Toiletries <li> and the next <li>
Inside the Toiletries <li>, before its closing tag
After the outer , indented to look nested
Inside the outer <ul> but outside any <li>
html-b16-lists.why: A nested list belongs to an item, so it must sit inside that item's li. Lists may only contain li elements directly — a ul as a direct child of another ul is invalid.

html-b17-description-lists.q: You are building a product spec panel: 'Weight: 1.2 kg', 'Battery: 14 h', 'Ports: 2x USB-C'. Which structure fits this name-value content?
options: A ul with the pairs joined by colons in each li
A dl with each label as a dt and each value as a dd
An ol so the specs stay in order
html-b17-description-lists.why: Name-value pairs are exactly what description lists express: the pairing lives in the markup itself. In a ul the colon does the pairing visually only, invisible to machines.

html-b17-description-lists.q: In a glossary, the term 'HTTP' needs two separate descriptions. What is the valid markup?
options: One <dd> containing both texts separated by <dt>
It is not possible — dl allows exactly one dd per dt
html-b17-description-lists.why: Any number of dd elements may follow a dt, and all of them describe it. Duplicating the term creates two entries, and dt inside dd is invalid.

html-b17-description-lists.q: A colleague wraps plain paragraphs of text directly inside <dl> to get indentation. What is wrong with that?
options: dl may directly contain only dt and dd (plus div wrappers); prose belongs inside dd, and indentation is a CSS job
dl is deprecated and should be replaced with ul
The paragraphs will not render at all
html-b17-description-lists.why: Loose content inside dl is invalid: its direct children are dt and dd (div is allowed as a grouping wrapper). Using dl for visual indentation misuses semantics that CSS handles properly.

html-b18-block-inline.q:
You write

Closing date:

Friday

and the layout breaks strangely. Why?
options: div is deprecated inside modern HTML
A p may contain only inline content, so the parser closes the paragraph early when it meets the div
The div needs a class before it can be nested
Paragraphs cannot contain any child elements
html-b18-block-inline.why: Block elements are invalid inside p, and the parser repairs the markup by ending the paragraph before the div — silently changing your structure. An inline span is the correct wrapper there.

html-b18-block-inline.q: You need to highlight two words in the middle of a sentence so CSS can color them, without breaking the text flow. Which element fits?
options: <section>, to mark the words as a section
html-b18-block-inline.why: span is the meaningless inline wrapper made exactly for styling a run of text mid-sentence. div, section and p are block-level and would break the line.

html-b18-block-inline.q: Three product cards each consist of an h2, a paragraph and a link, and each card needs a border around all three. What is the standard approach?
options: Wrap each card's elements in a <div class="card"> and style the class
Give the h2, p and a identical inline borders
Wrap each card in a <span class="card">
Put the three elements of each card inside one
html-b18-block-inline.why: A div groups block content into one styleable unit — one class rule then borders every card. A span may not contain blocks, and a p may not contain an h2.

html-b19-classes-ids.q: Twelve warning paragraphs across a site must share one style, and one specific section needs a deep link. Which labeling is right?
options: id="warning" on all twelve, class="section" on the link target
class="warning" on the twelve paragraphs, id on the one link-target section
class on the section, ids on the paragraphs
Both attributes on everything, to be safe
html-b19-classes-ids.why: Classes are reusable labels for many elements; ids are unique per page and are what fragment links target. Twelve identical ids would be invalid and would break linking.

html-b19-classes-ids.q: An element must be both a note and highlighted as important. Which markup applies both classes?
html-b19-classes-ids.why: One class attribute holds multiple names separated by spaces. Repeating the attribute is invalid (browsers keep only the first), and commas are not separators.

html-b19-classes-ids.q: In CSS you write #signup { ... } but nothing changes. The element is <h2 class="signup">. What went wrong?
options: The selector is correct; the browser cache is stale
# selects by id, but the element only has a class — the selector should be .signup (or the element needs id="signup")
html-b19-classes-ids.why: The hash prefix matches ids and the dot prefix matches classes — they are not interchangeable. The attribute in the HTML must match the selector type in the CSS.

html-b20-styles-css-intro.q: A 40-page site needs one consistent design that can be updated in a single place. Where should the CSS live?
options: In style attributes on each element
In a <style> block copied into every page's head
In one external .css file referenced by <link rel="stylesheet"> from every page
In the footer of each page
html-b20-styles-css-intro.why: An external stylesheet is shared, cached and edited in one place. Inline styles and per-page style blocks duplicate the design 40 times and drift out of sync.

html-b20-styles-css-intro.q: Which line correctly attaches an external stylesheet?
html-b20-styles-css-intro.why: link is a void element in the head whose rel names the relationship and href locates the file. The style element has no src attribute, and there is no css element.

html-b20-styles-css-intro.q: A linked stylesheet sets p { color: black; }, a style block later in the head sets p { color: green; }, and one paragraph has style="color: red;". What color is that paragraph?
options: Black, because the external file loads first
Green, because style blocks always win
Red, because inline style attributes sit at the top of the cascade
The browser default, because the rules conflict
html-b20-styles-css-intro.why: Inline styles override both style blocks and linked stylesheets. Among the other two, the later, equally specific rule (green) would win — but the inline red outranks them both.

html-b21-colors.q: A designer's handoff specifies the brand color as #ff6b35. What does that notation encode?
options: Two hexadecimal digits each for the red, green and blue channels
A named color from the CSS keyword list
A transparency value followed by a color code
html-b21-colors.why: A six-digit hex code is three byte pairs — red ff, green 6b, blue 35 — each running 00 to ff. Hue and saturation belong to hsl() notation, and names contain no digits.

html-b21-colors.q: You need the brand teal as a 30%-opacity overlay on a photo, letting the photo show through. Which value does that?
html-b21-colors.why: The alpha channel in rgba() sets opacity — 0.3 lets the underlying image show through. A paler solid color would hide the photo, and the other syntaxes are invalid.

html-b21-colors.q: A hero section has background-color: #e8e8e8 with color: #f5f5f5 text, and users complain they cannot read it. What is the actual problem?
options: hex colors cannot be used for text
The contrast ratio between two near-identical light grays is far below the 4.5:1 readability target
The background should have been rgb() instead
Text needs a named color to render
html-b21-colors.why: Readability is about the difference between text and background — two light grays give a ratio near 1:1. The notation is irrelevant; the pair needs genuine dark-on-light or light-on-dark contrast.

html-b22-head-title-meta.q: A client's page shows perfectly but its browser tab reads 'Untitled Document' and Google shows the bare URL as its headline. What is missing?
html-b22-head-title-meta.why: The title element feeds the tab label, bookmarks and the search-result headline. The h1 is visible page content and does not label the tab.

html-b22-head-title-meta.q: On phones your page renders zoomed out, like a shrunken desktop screenshot. Which single line fixes it?
html-b22-head-title-meta.why: Without the viewport meta, phone browsers render onto an imaginary desktop-width canvas and zoom out. width=device-width tells them to use the screen's true width.

html-b22-head-title-meta.q: You want to control the gray snippet Google shows under your search result. Which markup targets it?
options: <meta name="description" content="One clear sentence about the page.">
html-b22-head-title-meta.why: The description meta supplies the snippet text. The keywords meta is ignored by modern search engines, there is no description element, and the title becomes the headline, not the snippet.

html-b23-charsets-entities.q: A page saved as UTF-8 displays â‚¬ where € should appear on some visitors' machines. What is the root cause?
options: The euro sign is not part of UTF-8
No charset was declared, so those browsers guessed the wrong decoding table
The euro sign must always be written as an image
html-b23-charsets-entities.why: Without <meta charset="UTF-8">, browsers guess the encoding, and a wrong guess decodes the euro's multi-byte sequence as garbage characters. Declaring the charset pins the decoding everywhere.

html-b23-charsets-entities.q: A tutorial page must display the literal text <h1> as content. How is it written in the source?
html-b23-charsets-entities.why: Angle brackets meant as text must be the entities < and >, each ending with a semicolon — otherwise the parser opens a real h1 element. Backslashes escape nothing in HTML.

html-b23-charsets-entities.q: Prices like '25 €' keep line-breaking between the number and the symbol. What is the correct fix?
options: Write 25 € so the space cannot break
Replace the space with a hyphen
html-b23-charsets-entities.why: The non-breaking space renders as a space but forbids wrapping at that point. Multiple normal spaces collapse into one when rendered, and bold has no effect on line breaking.

html-b24-project-profile-page.q: Planning your profile page, you settle on: name, then About, Skills and Contact sections. Which heading assignment is correct?
options: h1 for the name; h2 for About, Skills and Contact
h1 for everything, styled to different sizes
h1 for the name; h3 for the sections because h2 looks too big
h2 for the name; h1 for each section
html-b24-project-profile-page.why: One h1 states what the page is about (you), and each major section sits one level below as an h2. Skipping to h3 for looks breaks the outline — size is a CSS decision.

html-b24-project-profile-page.q: Your profile's GitHub link is GitHub. A code review flags it. What is the accepted fix?
options: Move the link into the head
html-b24-project-profile-page.why: Every target="_blank" link should carry rel="noopener" so the opened page cannot script the opener — the standard review comment for external profile links.

html-b24-project-profile-page.q: You want '© 2026 Alex Petrou' in the footer and a private note in the source for your future self. Which pair is correct?
options: © 2026 in the text, and <!-- update projects next --> as the note
(c) 2026 in the text, and <note>update projects</note> in the body
&copyright 2026 in the text, and // update projects as the note
©right; in the text, and /* update projects */ in the body
html-b24-project-profile-page.why: © is the named entity for the copyright symbol, and HTML comments use the <!-- --> syntax, invisible to visitors. Slashes and /* */ are comment styles from other languages, not HTML.
